quality_assessment: Chapter provides comprehensive coverage of file type filtering but contains several outdated or incorrect type definitions in the examples

issues.description: Chapter claims Python type includes BUILD, BUILD.bazel, SConstruct, Snakefile but this is inaccurate
issues.fix_suggestion: Update line 253 to show correct Python type definition. Note that BUILD files are part of the 'bazel' type, not 'python'

issues.description: Chapter claims CSS type includes *.sass but it only includes *.css and *.scss
issues.fix_suggestion: Update line 265 to remove *.sass. Note there is a separate 'sass' type that includes *.sass and *.scss

issues.description: Chapter doesn't mention that js type also includes *.vue files
issues.fix_suggestion: Update line 256 to include *.vue in the list

issues.description: Chapter shows simplified Ruby type definition but omits several patterns
issues.fix_suggestion: Update line 260 to show more complete Ruby type definition or note it's simplified

issues.description: Chapter doesn't mention that some types have aliases (e.g., 'py' is an alias for 'python', 'md' for 'markdown', 'ts' for 'typescript')
issues.should_add: Add note explaining that some types have short aliases, with examples like py→python, md→markdown, ts→typescript, js→javascript
issues.fix_suggestion: Add subsection or note in 'Built-in File Types' section explaining aliases and how to discover them via --type-list
issues.source_reference: crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs:217 (shows py,python as array of names)

issues.description: Chapter claims 150+ built-in types, but current count is 218
issues.current_content: Ripgrep ships with 150+ built-in file types
issues.should_be: Ripgrep ships with 200+ built-in file types (218 as of current version)
issues.fix_suggestion: Update line 3 to reflect current count (200+ is safer than exact number which may change). Alternatively, keep 150+ as conservative estimate

positive_aspects: Excellent structure with clear progression from basic to advanced
Comprehensive coverage of all type-related flags (-t, -T, --type-add, --type-clear)
Great practical examples showing real-world use cases
Short form syntax (-trust) correctly documented and explained
Correct explanation of type name constraints (alphanumeric only)
Accurate documentation of include: directive for composing types
Good troubleshooting section addressing common issues
Correct file path references for implementation details
Excellent comparison of when to use types vs globs
Configuration file persistence section is accurate and helpful
improvement_suggestions: Add a subsection explicitly covering type aliases with examples
Consider adding a table of the most commonly used types with their complete definitions
Add note that --type-list output shows the authoritative, up-to-date definitions
Include example showing how to check what a specific type includes (rg --type-list | grep rust)
Add cross-reference to the separate 'sass' type when discussing CSS type

metadata.validation_focus: Check that --type flag usage and custom type definitions are accurate
